title: Draft routing heuristics for staged speculative decode with attention-window profiling
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Propose and implement a lightweight staged routing heuristic that integrates runtime kernel selection signals, attention-window profiling, and an early-commit confidence estimator to enable safe speculative decoding. The goal is to reduce tail latency for short-to-medium responses while bounding cost and minimizing incorrect commits that require fallback rework.

Background: Our existing speculative routing work focuses on prefill probes and acceptance thresholds but lacks an integrated signal from kernel suitability and attention window characteristics. We see cases where the fast-path model and kernel produce low-quality tentative tokens when the attention span of the request grows past the profiled distribution; conversely, oversized kernel allocations increase latency unnecessarily.

Goals: 
- Reduce 95th/99th token latency for interactive workloads by 15% on average for queries with expected length <= 128 tokens.
- Keep speculative commit reverts (cases where tentative tokens are discarded and full decode retried) below 1.5% of speculative attempts in production for non-adversarial workloads.
- Ensure no customer-facing semantic regressions (tracked via held-out eval prompts).

Scope: 
- Design heuristic that combines: kernel-affinity score (based on kernel fingerprints and sequence-length performance curves), attention-window profile (quick estimate from prompt/prefix tokens), and a confidence-on-first-k-tokens estimator (lightweight classifier that predicts acceptance probability).
- Implement a staging controller: Stage 0 = optimistic fast-path; Stage 1 = guarded fast-path with small KV prefetch; Stage 2 = full decode. Heuristics decide initial stage and transitions.
- Add telemetry: routed_model, kernel_fingerprint, attention_window_estimate, acceptance_score, commit_outcome, cost_delta, latency_by_stage.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Unit and integration tests covering stage transitions and fallback correctness.
- Canary rollout with throttled traffic on runtime-1.20 infra, monitoring the five telemetry keys and automated rollback if commit_revert_rate > 2% or tail latency regresses beyond SLA.
- PR with code and a design doc linked; design doc reviewed by two runtime engineers and one product PM.

Design notes: 
- Kernel-affinity: runtime maintains a small table mapping kernel_fingerprint -> observed per-sequence-length p95/p99. The heuristic uses an interpolated penalty when sequence length estimate exceeds the knee point.
- Attention-window profiling: quick estimator inspects prompt length and recent usage to choose an attention-mode (short, mid, long) and adjusts kernel-affinity weighting.
- Confidence estimator: a tiny linear model (logistic) trained on previously observed probe features (first token logits entropy, top-k concentration, delta-per-token) executed in C++ in the decoder hot-path to avoid Python overhead. Model is versioned and gated.
- Conservative defaults: when any signal is missing fallback to Stage 1. When confidence is low and predicted length > 256, directly choose Stage 2.

Trade-offs and rationale: 
- Added complexity in runtime vs. reduced tail latency and cost. Keep heuristic interpretable to allow ops overrides.
- Using a tiny classifier reduces miscommit rate but adds micro-latency; chosen features and implementation minimize the overhead (<200us median).

Operational plan: 
1) Implement heuristic and feature toggle behind runtime flag (spec.decode.staged_routing_v1).
2) Run offline simulation using 14 days of sampled traffic to estimate revert rates and latency impact.
3) Canary on 5% of traffic with focused workloads (chat, search summaries).
4) Gradual ramp with metric checkpoints.

- Simulation notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/sim/staged-routing-analysis-2026-02.ipynb
